blocks.text: Ernest Rutherford's experiments in 1911 showed that an atom has a dense, positively charged central part, the nucleus, of very small size, surrounded by electrons. In 1920 Rutherford suggested that the positive charge is due to protons in the nucleus and predicted another particle with no charge; the prediction came true when James Chadwick discovered the neutron in 1932.

Nuclear physics studies atomic nuclei and sub-atomic particles. This chapter discusses unstable nuclei that give off radiation, their decay, and nuclear reactions such as fission and fusion, which benefit mankind by releasing huge amounts of energy. Radioactive isotopes are used as tracers in medical diagnosis and treatment, agriculture, research and industry.

A nucleus, often called a nuclide, is written with the symbol X with mass number A and atomic (charge) number Z, where X is the chemical symbol, Z the number of protons and A the total number of nucleons (protons plus neutrons). The number of neutrons is N = A - Z. So hydrogen, carbon and uranium are written 1-1-H, 12-6-C and 235-92-U. The nucleus is very dense, with a radius of the order of 10^-14 m, surrounded by a cloud of electrons; the atomic radius is of the order of 10^-10 m.

blocks.title: Do you know?
blocks.text: From alpha-particle scattering experiments, Lord Rutherford concluded that most of an atom is empty and that its mass is concentrated in a very small region called the nucleus.
